title: e2e-test skill wiring — non-blocking review follow-up
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #105 (skill-e2e-testing), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: `.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md`'s new step 9a says a non-flake failing e2e spec is "review-blocking", while `.claude/agents/task-qa-reviewer.md`'s new step 5a says the same underlying signal is "at least a `major` gap" (task-qa-reviewer's severity scale is blocker/major/minor, and 5a doesn't say which of those a failing e2e spec collapses to when it's more severe than baseline `major` — e.g. one that contradicts Analyse.md/API.md would otherwise qualify as `blocker` per step 6's own definition). Not a defect introduced by this PR specifically (the two agents already phrase other shared checks slightly differently elsewhere), but worth reconciling explicitly so a task-qa-reviewer run doesn't under-rank a failure that pr-reviewer would treat as an outright block.

decisions.decision: Changed `.claude/agents/task-qa-reviewer.md` step 5a so a non-flake failing e2e spec always maps to severity `blocker` in task-qa-reviewer's blocker/major/minor scale, rather than "at least `major`" with an undefined escalation condition.
decisions.rationale: Step 6's own scale defines `blocker` as breaking the feature or contradicting Analyse.md/API.md, and `major` as 'works but missing required coverage/error-handling/tests'. A non-flake e2e failure (per the e2e-test skill's own flake-vs-regression guidance in its step 4: 'the app's actual behavior changed and a spec's assertion is now correct-and-failing') is by definition the app actually being broken in a real browser+backend run, not merely under-tested — so it fits `blocker`'s definition, not `major`'s, in every case, not just some. Considered instead defining an explicit escalation condition (e.g. 'major, escalating to blocker if the failing spec covers a golden path or contradicts Analyse.md/API.md') to preserve a `major` floor, but rejected it: nearly every persisted e2e spec covers a golden path by design (per the e2e-test skill, the suite is exactly the golden-path specs for dashboard/navigation/portfolio/stock-analysis), so the 'escalates' branch would fire almost universally anyway, making a conditional rule more complex than a flat one for no practical difference. A flat `blocker` also removes the ambiguity the task flagged and matches `pr-reviewer` step 9a's unconditional 'review-blocking' treatment of the identical signal, so a task-qa-reviewer run and a pr-reviewer run never disagree on how severe the same failing spec is.
